title: Pennsylvania's 2nd Congressional District election, 2026
description: Pennsylvania's 2nd Congressional District, covering all of Northeast Philadelphia and parts of North Philadelphia and Center City east of Broad Street, is holding its general election on November 3, 2026. The race pits incumbent Democratic U.S. Rep. Brendan Boyle, who has represented the district since 2019 and serves as Ranking Member of the House Budget Committee, against Republican challenger Jessica Arriaga, a healthcare professional and community health coordinator making her first run for elected office. The district is overwhelmingly Democratic by partisan registration, and the Cook Political Report rated the seat as 'Solidly Democratic' heading into the primary. Key issues in the race include economic opportunity, healthcare access, public safety, and the cost of living in Philadelphia.
polling_note: No independent general-election opinion polls were found for Pennsylvania's 2nd Congressional District in 2026. The Cook Political Report rated the race 'Solidly Democratic' before the primary, and prediction markets indicate a high probability of a Democratic win in this heavily Democratic Philadelphia-based district.

candidates.name: Brendan Boyle
candidates.summary: Brendan Boyle is an incumbent Democratic U.S. Representative for Pennsylvania's 2nd Congressional District, first elected in 2014 after serving in the Pennsylvania House of Representatives. He serves as the Ranking Member of the House Budget Committee and focuses on fiscal policy, healthcare access, and economic opportunity. Boyle was born and raised in Philadelphia and is the first in his family to attend college, earning degrees from the University of Notre Dame and Harvard Kennedy School.

candidates.name: Jessica Arriaga
candidates.summary: Jessica Arriaga is a Republican candidate running for U.S. House representing Pennsylvania's 2nd Congressional District. She has worked as an operating room technician for over 20 years and later expanded into community health coordination in North Philadelphia. Born and raised in North Philadelphia to a Puerto Rican family, Arriaga is an evangelical Christian and serves as the Republican Ward Leader for Philadelphia's 37th District, making her first bid for elected office.

forecast.rationale: No independent general-election polls are available for this race, so confidence is low. However, the race data describes PA-02 as an overwhelmingly Democratic Philadelphia-based district by partisan registration. Incumbent Brendan Boyle has held the seat since 2014, serves as Ranking Member of the House Budget Committee, and faces a first-time Republican challenger with no elected office experience. The Cook Political Report rated the seat 'Solidly Democratic' heading into the primary. Absent any evidence of unusual competitiveness, structural factors point to an overwhelming Democratic advantage.
